name: London System
description: 1.d4 and 2.Bf4, then the same e3, c3, Nbd2 and Bd3 set-up against almost anything.

lines.name: Main Line vs …d5, …c5

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.8: c3 holds the d4 pawn firmly against …c5.
notes.12: Bg3 keeps the bishop when …Bd6 offers a trade, and opens the h-file if Black takes.
notes.14: Bd3 aims at Black's king; Ne5 and a kingside attack can follow.

lines.summary: Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nbd2, Bd3: the London pyramid, the same set-up every time.

lines.name: Ne5 and f4

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.8: c3 holds the d4 pawn firmly against …c5.
notes.12: Bg3 keeps the bishop when …Bd6 offers a trade, and opens the h-file if Black takes.
notes.14: Bd3 aims at Black's king; Ne5 and a kingside attack can follow.
notes.16: Ne5 grabs the outpost and starts a kingside attack.
notes.18: f4 supports the e5 knight, a Stonewall-style attacking set-up.

lines.summary: When Black plays slowly, put a knight on e5, back it with f4 and attack the king.

lines.name: vs 4…Bd6

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.8: Bg3 keeps the bishop; if Black takes, hxg3 opens the h-file.
notes.10: Bd3 aims at h7, as in the main line.

lines.summary: Against …Bd6, retreat to g3 instead of trading, then Bd3 and the usual pyramid.

lines.name: 4…Bd6 into the main line

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.8: Bg3 keeps the bishop; if Black takes, hxg3 opens the h-file.
notes.10: Bd3 aims at h7, as in the main line.
notes.14: Nbd2: the same position as the main line.

lines.summary: …Bd6 and …c5 bring us to the main line: Bg3, Bd3, c3, Nbd2.

lines.name: vs 3…Bf5

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.6: Bd3 offers to trade off Black's best minor piece.

lines.summary: When Black copies with …Bf5, challenge the bishop with Bd3.

lines.name: 3…Bf5 4.Bd3 Bxd3

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.6: Bd3 offers to trade off Black's best minor piece.
notes.10: Nf3: the queen on d3 eyes h7 and supports a later e4.

lines.summary: After the bishop trade, develop with Nf3 and Nbd2 and prepare e4 with the queen on d3.

lines.name: vs 3…c5

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.14: Bd3: the same position as the main line.

lines.summary: Different move order, same London: keep building the pyramid.

lines.name: vs …c5 and …Qb6

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.9: …Qb6 attacks b2, which the f4 bishop no longer defends.
notes.10: Qb3 offers a queen trade that would open the a-file for White's rook.
notes.12: Qc2 keeps the queen; White wants e4 next to break the black centre.

lines.summary: Meet …Qb6 with Qb3 (or Qc2); if …c4 kicks the queen, go to c2 and aim for e4.

lines.name: vs 2…e6

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.6: Nf3: the same position as 2…Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3.

lines.summary: 2…e6 changes nothing: e3, Nf3, and the usual pyramid.

lines.name: vs 2…Nc6

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.6: Nf3: develop as usual; c3 and Bd3 come next.

lines.summary: Against 2…Nc6, keep the same set-up: e3, Nf3, then c3 and Bd3.

lines.name: vs 2…c5

notes.2: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 shuts it in.
notes.4: e3 backs up d4 and keeps the set-up.
notes.14: Bd3: the same position as the main line.

lines.summary: 2…c5 changes nothing: build the same pyramid and you reach the main line.

lines.name: vs King's Indian set-up

notes.4: e3 supports d4 and frees the f1 bishop.
notes.8: Be2 is the usual square here: against …g6 the bishop has little to aim at on d3.
notes.10: h3 gives the f4 bishop a retreat on h2, so …Nh5 can't trade it.

lines.summary: Against …g6, keep the pyramid, put the bishop on e2 and play h3 to save the f4 bishop.

lines.name: vs King's Indian: 6…Nbd7

notes.4: e3 supports d4 and frees the f1 bishop.
notes.8: Be2 is the usual square here: against …g6 the bishop has little to aim at on d3.
notes.10: h3 gives the f4 bishop a retreat on h2, so …Nh5 can't trade it.
notes.12: O-O: if Black plays …e5, the f4 bishop drops back to h2 and keeps its diagonal.

lines.summary: Against …Nbd7 and …e5 ideas, just castle; the h2 square keeps your bishop safe.
